sectionAppendix.dataContract: Added sample records and schedules are illustrative. Research snapshots are historical. Decorative mini-charts are not performance history. Content generation and live publishing are not configured. The AI visibility database is provisioned; app authentication, cloud sync, collection, and scheduling remain unconnected. Original composer changes are session-only; the AI prompt library has separate browser-local persistence as recorded in aiPlanning.

appearance.lightValues: Original per-component CSS fallbacks; layout and typography unchanged.

aiPlanning.stage: Local website intake and AI Insights foundation; existing Dashboard 2 visual system preserved. Supabase schema provisioned with RLS; app authentication/cloud sync, collection, scheduling, and deployment remain pending.
aiPlanning.patterns: Soft summary panel, two real local counts, connection disclosure, inline editor, status filters, search/topic toolbar, horizontally contained table, native Settings disclosures.
aiPlanning.behavior: Save curated suggestions or up to 30 questions, edit, prevent duplicates, filter by topic/search, archive/restore, export saved and archived rows as CSV.
aiPlanning.boundary: Business context and prompts stay on this device. Original global prompt key remains untouched. Normal Insights measurements are empty; opt-in synthetic records drive labelled previews, filters, evidence and JSON export. Synthetic data never writes to the backend.
connectors: Supabase: Backend provisioned; sign-in/cloud sync unconnected
Optional and unconnected: GA4, Search Console, website request logs, CMS publishing
aiPlanning.theme: Every new --d2-* reference has a light fallback because semantic declarations are dark-only.
aiPlanning.responsive: At 650px and below, connection disclosure becomes a full-width row; editor fields and toolbar stack. Existing shell and contained table scrolling remain.
aiPlanning.monitoringDirection: Independent monitoring, initially Uplift AI; Searchable supplies feature and composition references only. Dashboard 2 owns the aesthetic. Live collection still needs authorized engine access and a budget. Record engine, method, and capture time; distinguish API responses from consumer search results.
aiPlanning.insightsLayout: Website intake uses a 1.6:1 two-panel grid; non-Visibility analysis uses 1.18:1. These grids stack at 1000px. At 650px panels use 21px padding and filters form two columns. Visibility has its own equal two-column report grid, recorded in visibilityReport. Soft panels, Inter, lavender actions and existing light/dark roles remain. Sentiment bars scale proportionally from zero with visible counts.

visibilityReport.authority: User video structure, adapted to existing Dashboard 2 material and palette; no new design tokens.
visibilityReport.toolbar: Find brand, Learn, Export; seven existing AI Insights tabs retained.
visibilityReport.filters: Brand, date and daily/weekly cadence separated from prompt type, model, topic and location.
visibilityReport.layout: Equal two-by-two grid: Visibility and Rankings above Avg position and Share of voice; 22px gutter, compact 14px headings and 27px values. Trend SVGs respond to container width with 12px axis labels.
visibilityReport.behavior: Visibility bars/trend toggle with optional comparison lines; brand selection; rankings sortable by visibility, share of voice, sentiment and average position; position trend/table toggle; share-of-voice donut/trend toggle.
visibilityReport.details: Native right-aligned dialog, width min(1440px, 84vw), 16px insets; three-metric brand summary, comparison trend, searchable sortable comparison table.
visibilityReport.responsive: At 900px report panels stack and dialog uses 10px viewport insets. At 650px toolbar wraps and filters form two columns. Tables scroll within their containers.
visibilityReport.boundary: Six synthetic preview brands with visible sample disclosure; normal measurements remain empty. No live collection or backend write is implied. Website-first intake is unchanged.

narrative.overview: This system records the implemented Uplift AI dashboard in React and Vite. Its visual authority is the user's selected screen inside the Clinexa laptop reference, adapted to Uplift's content operations terminology. The cool lavender-to-mint canvas, soft white panels, compact Inter typography, purple icon rail, and pastel charts follow that selection; this is not a newly invented visual identity.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet tonal separation between the canvas and panels.
Compact text with large, steady metric numerals.
Rounded controls, slim SVG icons, and pastel data graphics.
A dense desktop overview that stacks into a mobile workspace.

rules.name: The Labeled Data Rule
rules.body: Pair chart colors and status dots with text; preserve the visible illustrative-data and snapshot labels.

rules.name: The Overlay Depth Rule
rules.body: Reserve substantial shadow and backdrop blur for content that floats over the workspace.

rules.name: The Local Evidence Rule
rules.body: Keep local business context, planning counts, historical snapshots, synthetic previews, and collected measurements visibly distinct. Default AI Insights to empty until answer evidence exists. Saving a question does not collect AI answers, register monitoring, or create a live connection.

rules.name: The Theme Fallback Rule
rules.body: New AI research and connector styles consume the existing dark-only `--d2-*` semantic roles with an explicit light fallback at every reference. Preserve the incumbent Inter, lavender actions, soft panels, and unchanged shell in both appearances.

dos: **Do** preserve the user-selected Clinexa screen's quiet palette and dashboard hierarchy.
**Do** retain readable card titles and metadata when adapting density.
**Do** pair interactive chart marks with keyboard focus behavior and textual values.
**Do** distinguish historical workspace snapshots, illustrative charts, and session-only changes.
donts: **Don't** import the original Uplift website's layout or imagery into this reference-led dashboard.
**Don't** replace SVG and CSS data graphics with raster approximations.
**Don't** treat the smallest auxiliary annotations as the default text scale for new components.
**Don't** imply that a preview interaction publishes content or changes a live connection.
